scenario.title: 護照、錢包不見了，推理它在哪
scenario.context: 東西不見時，大家會開始推理：「一定是掉在計程車上了」「可能被偷了」「不可能在飯店，我有檢查」。這些「對過去的推測」要用 must have / might have / can't have + p.p.，是第 35 單元 must 推測的過去版本。

lines.speaker: Minz
lines.en: Jess, I can't find my passport. I'm starting to freak out.
lines.zh: Jess，我找不到護照，我開始慌了。

lines.speaker: Jess
lines.en: OK, keep your cool. When did you last have it?
lines.zh: 好，冷靜。你最後一次拿到它是什麼時候？

lines.speaker: Minz
lines.en: At the hotel check-in. I must have left it at the front desk.
lines.zh: 飯店入住的時候。我一定是把它留在櫃台了。

lines.speaker: Jess
lines.en: Or you might have put it in your backpack. Did you check the side pocket?
lines.zh: 或者你可能放進背包了。你有檢查側袋嗎？

lines.speaker: Minz
lines.en: I did. It can't have been in my backpack. I emptied the whole thing.
lines.zh: 檢查了。不可能在背包，我整個倒出來了。

lines.speaker: Jess
lines.en: Let's call the hotel before we panic.

lines.speaker: Minz
lines.en: Good idea. I completely lost track of it after the taxi.
lines.zh: 好主意。下計程車後我就完全不記得它去哪了。

lines.speaker: Clerk
lines.en: Hello, front desk. How can I help?
lines.zh: 您好，這裡是櫃台，有什麼需要？

lines.speaker: Minz
lines.en: Hi, I checked in this afternoon. I think I might have left my passport at the desk.
lines.zh: 你好，我今天下午入住，我想我可能把護照留在櫃台了。

lines.speaker: Clerk
lines.en: Let me check. … Yes, we have a Taiwanese passport here. Someone must have put it in the safe.
lines.zh: 我查一下……有，我們這有一本台灣護照，應該是有人把它放進保險箱了。

lines.speaker: Minz
lines.en: Oh, thank goodness. I'll come down right now.
lines.zh: 喔，謝天謝地。我馬上下去。

lines.speaker: Jess
lines.en: See? I told you it would turn up.

lines.speaker: Minz
lines.en: You were right. I must have looked like a crazy person.
lines.zh: 你是對的。我剛剛一定看起來像個瘋子。

patterns.en: When did you last have it?
patterns.zh: 你最後一次拿到是什麼時候？

patterns.en: I must have left it in the taxi.
patterns.zh: 我一定是忘在計程車上了。

patterns.en: Someone might have taken it by mistake.
I'd like to report a lost ___.

chinglish.wrong: My passport is lost by me.
chinglish.right: I lost my passport. / I can't find my passport.
chinglish.why: 被動句聽起來很怪。直接用主動 I lost… 最自然。

chinglish.wrong: I must left it in the taxi.
chinglish.right: I must have left it in the taxi.
chinglish.why: 推測過去要用 must have + p.p.，不能直接接過去式。

chinglish.wrong: It mustn't be in my bag.
chinglish.right: It can't be in my bag. / It can't have been in my bag.
chinglish.why: 推測否定用 can't（複習第 35 單元），mustn't 是「禁止」。

chinglish.wrong: Don't be nervous, calm down calm down.
chinglish.right: Stay calm. We'll figure it out.
chinglish.why: 重複說 calm down 反而讓人更緊張，英文會給具體的安撫。

grammar.title: 推測過去 must / might / can't have
grammar.oneLiner: 情態動詞 + have + p.p. 用來推測「過去」發生了什麼：must have（一定是）、might / could have（可能）、can't have（不可能）。
whenToUse: must have + p.p.：很有把握的推測。I must have left it at the desk.
might / may / could have + p.p.：不確定的推測。Someone might have taken it.
can't / couldn't have + p.p.：很有把握的否定推測。It can't have been stolen. The door was locked.
口語縮寫：must've, might've, could've（聽起來像 must of，但寫法是 have）。
比較：must be（推測現在）vs must have been（推測過去）。
grammar.whyWeGetItWrong: 中文推測過去只要加「一定是」「可能」，後面動詞直接用：「一定是掉了」「可能被偷了」。英文的情態動詞後面只能接原形，所以要表示過去，就得靠 have + p.p. 來承載時間。台灣人常說 must left 或 might lost，就是把中文的結構直接套進來。

examples.correct: I must have dropped it on the train.
examples.incorrect: I must dropped it on the train.

examples.correct: She might have gone home already.
He can't have seen us. He didn't wave.
You must be tired. You must have walked ten kilometers today.
examples.note: must be（現在）vs must have walked（過去）。
常用的安慰句：本來可能更糟。

quiz.question: My wallet's gone. I ___ it on the bus.
It ___ been stolen. I had it in my hand the whole time.
I'm not sure. Someone ___ have picked it up by mistake.
You look exhausted. You must have ___ (walk) all day.
Which is correct?
quiz.explanation: 寫作時是 must have，不是 must of。

slang.meaning: 搞不清楚、忘了注意（時間、東西、人）
slang.usage: lose track of time（忘了時間）、lose track of someone（跟某人失聯）。

examples.en: Sorry, I lost track of time. Am I late?
examples.zh: 抱歉，我忘了時間，我遲到了嗎？

examples.en: I lost track of my keys somewhere between the café and home.
examples.zh: 從咖啡店到家的路上，我不知道鑰匙丟哪了。

slang.usage: freak out / be freaking out / freak someone out（嚇到某人）。

examples.en: I freaked out when I couldn't find my passport.
examples.zh: 找不到護照時我整個嚇壞了。

examples.en: Don't freak out, but I think I broke your mug.
examples.zh: 你先別抓狂，但我好像打破你的杯子了。

slang.usage: 在壓力下不慌、不生氣。反義 lose your cool（失控、發火）。

examples.en: She kept her cool even when the client started yelling.
examples.zh: 客戶開始吼的時候她還是很冷靜。

examples.en: I lost my cool and said something I regret.
examples.zh: 我失控說了讓我後悔的話。

slang.usage: It'll turn up. = 它會出現的。也指人突然出現：He turned up late.

risk.note: 另外 turn up 也有「把音量調大」的意思（第 33 單元 Turn it up!）。

examples.en: Don't worry about your ring. It'll turn up.
examples.zh: 別擔心你的戒指，它會出現的。

examples.en: Only five people turned up to the meeting.

review.question: If I ___ my passport, I'd go straight to the embassy.
review.explanation: 複習第 45 單元：type 2 用過去式。

review.question: I recommend ___ a photo of your passport.
My bag got ___ (leave) on the train.
I blamed ___ for losing it.
review.explanation: 複習第 38 單元：反身代名詞。

review.question: I ___ my keys three times this month!
review.explanation: 複習第 30 單元：到現在為止的次數用現在完成式。

review.question: Which is correct?
options: I must left it at home.
I must have left it at home.
I must leaving it at home.
